base_member_text: rmse() (L49) is not defined here; requires external function.
audit_member_text: The rmse call at line 49 relies on a function not defined in this file; compatibility depends on an external MATLAB/toolbox or path-provided implementation.

base_member_text: Measured records are raw gauge units while the model is converted to cm (L9); the comparison at L44-46 assumes r2d*.dat are already in cm -- units not verifiable from this file (the companion fft script applies scale_fac=0.01 to the same r2d470.dat).
z (L8), model_time (L12), num inside the second loop (L31), and data_time (L36) are computed but never used; the variable name error shadows MATLAB's built-in error function (L49).

No time-window alignment or truncation is applied before std comparison (unlike comp_mkskew.m's 400-sample cut) -- model and data records of different lengths/durations are compared whole; whether that is intended cannot be resolved here.
The fnam column order (L17-28) maps measured files by depth to gauge index; the deepest gauge column 1 (r2d470) is loaded but excluded by the shift at L37-39.

audit_member_text: relative_error is assigned without a k subscript at line 46 inside the 11-iteration loop on lines 41-47, so every iteration overwrites the preceding result and only the k=11 value survives; this is inconsistent with the indexed std_data and std_model outputs on lines 44-45.

Lines 7-12 overwrite gage for each numerical station and take time/model_time only from the final station. Those coordinates are never used when standard deviations are compared at lines 41-49, and the separately synthesized data_time at line 36 is also unused, so no sampling interval, duration, or time alignment check connects the two data sources.

Lines 44-46 divide by std_data(k) with no zero/non-finite guard, and line 49 divides by max(std_data) with no zero/non-finite guard; constant, empty, or invalid input can yield NaN or Inf and defeat the error metric.

num is recomputed at line 31 but is not used by the experimental-file load at line 32, which instead indexes fnam; this is a copy/paste residue and can falsely suggest that the numeric suffix controls the file mapping.

The filename table is written by column at lines 17-28 and each column is passed directly to load at line 32. The file does not establish whether the target MATLAB/Octave load interface accepts a column character vector; environments requiring a row character vector will reject fnam(:,k).

Lines 7-9 require every numerical file to have a second column and equal row count, while lines 32-33 require each experimental load to be a single compatible-length vector. None of these file-shape interfaces is checked.
